Listen to this article Share … as mining operators accuse marshals of extortion The House of Representatives Committee on Solid Minerals has summoned the Commandant-General of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) to appear before it within 24 hours over alleged N2 billion financial irregularities, unlawful arrests and harassment of licensed mining operators by the Mining Marshals. The committee also wants the NSCDC chief to explain the circumstances surrounding the death of Deputy Superintendent Agada Levi Agada, an NSCDC officer and member of the Mining Marshals, who was allegedly killed by fellow officers while on active duty at a mining site. The summons followed an investigative hearing convened by the committee to examine the activities, operations, funding and legal status of the Mining Marshals, a special security unit established to combat illegal mining across the country. Read also: Senate summons NCC, MTN, Airtel, others over poor network, unjustified airtime deductions The motion for the summons was moved by Ali Amburura, representing Sokoto State, and seconded by Majidi from Katsina State, following allegations of abuse of power, extortion, unlawful detention and financial misconduct by personnel of the unit. Gaza Gbefwi, Chairman of the Committee, said the investigation would examine an alleged N2 billion transaction linked to the bank account of a former state commander, suspected compromise within the Mining Marshals across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the Committee was also examining the Mining Marshals’ budgetary allocations, special intervention funds, vehicle procurement and other sources of financing to establish how the unit’s operations are funded and how the funds are utilised. Gbefwi recalled that more than 2,200 Mining Marshals were inaugurated in March 2024 to tackle illegal mining, curb the exploitation of mineral resources and strengthen security around mining locations nationwide. However, he stressed that the responsibility to protect the country’s mineral resources did not exempt the unit from operating within the law, respecting citizens’ fundamental rights and upholding accountability and professionalism. On the death of Agada, Obasi-Obi Nwabueze, presenting a petition on behalf of the family, said medical affidavits from doctors who attended to Agada contradicted the account that he died following an attack by bandits. Read also: Reps threaten arrest summons for Telcos’ CEOs over poor services According to him, Agada sustained a gunshot wound to the right side of his chest and was taken through two medical facilities before being transferred to the Federal Medical Centre, Keffi, where he eventually died. Nwabueze said the family became aware of the medical account after petitioning the Nigeria Police Force, adding that affidavits from the medical personnel involved were available to support their claims. He further alleged that two NSCDC officers were indicted in connection with the incident, while three officers were arrested during the police investigation. However, he claimed that the investigation was subsequently frustrated following the alleged arrest of the police officer handling the case and the withdrawal of the case file. The lawyer urged the Committee to intervene by ensuring that the Police conclude the criminal investigation and that anyone found culpable is brought to justice. He also sought protection for the deceased’s family and other witnesses, alleging that some had faced threats and intimidation. Agada, he disclosed, left behind a widow and two children aged 10 and seven. Responding, Gbefwi expressed the Committee’s condolences to the bereaved family and assured them that their petition would be forwarded to the appropriate authorities. He also requested an executive summary of the family’s submissions to guide the committee’s intervention. Read also: FCT Council chairs again shun Reps’ summons over N100bn audit query Meanwhile, licensed mining operators accused the Mining Marshals of unlawful arrests, prolonged detention and extortion. Rachel Ogbonna, Director of Communications at Stone Rockers Nigeria Limited, told the lawmakers that the company’s quarry site had remained sealed for more than one year despite possessing what she described as valid mining licences and operating documents. She alleged that 12 members of the company’s workforce were arrested and taken to an NSCDC detention facility along Airport Road. According to her, the company’s chairman and director were also detained after visiting the facility with relevant documents to establish the reasons for their employees’ arrest and secure their release. Ogbonna further alleged that the detainees were denied access to their lawyers, while the company’s director was prevented from receiving essential medication during his detention. She urged the Committee to scrutinise the Mining Marshals’ budgetary allocations, special intervention funds and other sources of financing, including expenditure on publications, publicity materials and operational activities. Read also: Reps summon Cardoso over unpaid pension arrears, alleged breach of CBN agreements In a separate submission, security operative Odey Cosmas Polycarp accused the Mining Marshals, allegedly led by one Onoja Attah, of arresting and detaining members of his workforce for several days while demanding N100 million for their release. Polycarp said the workers were arrested in a residential neighbourhood where no quarrying or mining activities were taking place, questioning the legal basis for their arrest and detention. He also alleged that the detained workers were repeatedly beaten while in custody, leaving them traumatised and fearful for their safety. He urged the lawmakers to investigate the allegations and hold any security operatives found responsible for extortion, abuse or unlawful detention accountable.
